storage.localOnlyTitle: Backups are only stored on this server
storage.localOnlyText: Backups on the same volume do not survive the loss of the disk or the server. Configure an external target under "External S3 copy" below so every backup is also stored elsewhere.
storage.title: Storage & keys

title: Backups
description: Full backups of the database and all stored files (images, invoices, tickets, bank statements). Backups are encrypted and kept in the local storage; an external S3 target is optional.
keyNote: Archives are encrypted with the key ring of this installation (key "{keyId}"). To restore a backup on another server, enter these keys there when restoring (or use the same APP_ENCRYPTION_KEYS) – keep a copy of them outside this system.

restore.title: Restore this backup?
restore.description: The database and all files are replaced by the state of {date}. A safety backup of the current state is created first; the shop is unavailable while the restore runs.
restore.descriptionDatabaseOnly: The database is replaced by the state of {date} (taken automatically before an update). Files such as images and ticket PDFs are not touched. A safety backup of the current state is created first; the shop is unavailable while the restore runs.
restore.lossTitle: Created after this backup and lost by the restore:
restore.lossNone: Nothing was created in the live system after this backup.
restore.gobd: Invoice and order numbers are never reused: the number counters keep the higher live values, so gaps may appear in the number sequence.
restore.acknowledge: I understand that data created after the backup is lost and that the system is unavailable during the restore.
restore.twoFactorSetup: Restoring requires two-factor authentication, but your account has none. Set up an authenticator app or a passkey first.
restore.passkeyHint: Instead of a code you can confirm with your passkey.
restore.secretKeysMissing: This backup holds secrets under encryption keys this system does not have ({keys}). Enter the key of the source system below, otherwise those secrets stay unreadable after the restore.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete this backup?
deleteConfirm.description: The backup is removed from this server and from the external target. This cannot be undone.
deleteConfirm.external: Also delete the copy on the external target

upload.hint: Restore a backup from another server or from the external target: upload the .tixbak file. It is checked completely before it appears in the list. For a backup of another system you need its encryption key (enter it in the upload dialog and again when restoring).
upload.accepted: Upload received – the file is being checked.
upload.notABackup: This file is not a backup archive.

dialog.title: Upload a backup file
dialog.description: Upload a .tixbak file, for example from another server or the external target. It is checked completely before it appears in the list.
dialog.keyHint: If this backup was made by another system, enter that system’s encryption key (the APP_ENCRYPTION_KEYS value of its .env file) below. Without it the file is rejected and deleted. The key is only used to check the file; you will be asked again when you restore it.
dialog.keyFailed: The entered key text is not valid.

settings.title: Schedule, retention and external copy
settings.description: Times use the shop time zone ({timeZone}).
settings.scheduleHint: A backup missed by more than six hours (e.g. the system was down) is skipped until the next slot.
settings.keepScheduledHint: Older scheduled backups are deleted, on the external target too. Manual backups are kept until you delete them.
settings.alertEmail: Alert e-mail for failed scheduled backups
settings.alertEmailHint: Sent through the configured mail server; failures also appear on the dashboard.

external.title: External S3 copy
external.enabled: Upload every backup to an external S3-compatible target
external.forcePathStyle: Path-style addressing (needed for MinIO and many providers)
external.replaceHint: Leave empty to keep the stored keys.
external.enterHint: Both keys are stored encrypted and are never shown again.

settings.manualMaxAgeDays: Delete manual and safety backups after (days)
settings.manualMaxAgeDaysHint: 0 = keep until deleted by hand. Backups contain personal data: a limit helps with erasure requests (GDPR Art. 17). The newest verified backup is never deleted. Erasures are replayed after a restore.
settings.allowPrivateNetwork: Allow endpoints in private networks (e.g. a MinIO on your LAN)
settings.credentialsChangeHint: Changing endpoint or bucket requires entering the keys again.

probe.title: Automatic probe restore
probe.hint: Restores into a temporary database, migrates and checks it, then deletes it. A failure is reported on the dashboard and by warning e-mail. The live database is not touched. Off by default: switch it on once the database server has free disk space of at least twice the database size.

feedback.connectionOk: Connection works: a test file was written, read and deleted.
feedback.busy: Another backup operation is running. Please wait until it has finished.
feedback.twoFactorRequired: Enter the code of your authenticator app (or a recovery code), or confirm with a passkey.
feedback.passkeyInvalid: The passkey could not be verified. Please try again.
feedback.acknowledge: Please confirm that you understand the consequences.
feedback.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Please wait a few minutes.
feedback.connectionIncomplete: Please enter endpoint, bucket and both access keys first.
feedback.endpointNotAllowed: This endpoint is not allowed: use https and a public address (or enable the matching option below).
feedback.protected: The newest verified backup cannot be deleted.
feedback.twoFactorSetupRequired: Restoring requires two-factor authentication. Set it up in your account first.
feedback.sourceKeysInvalid: The entered encryption key is not valid. Expected entries like id:base64, separated by commas or lines.
feedback.sourceKeysDisabled: Restoring with the key of another system is disabled on this server. The operator can enable it with TIX_ALLOW_FOREIGN_BACKUP_KEYS=1 (see the backup documentation).

incomplete.title: Restore incomplete – the system stays in maintenance mode
incomplete.text: The database was replaced but the restore did not finish (step: {step}). Run the restore again, or restore the safety backup that was taken before it.

probe.title: Automatic probe restore
probe.description: The newest backup is regularly restored into a temporary test database (never the live one), brought to the current database structure and checked. This proves that a backup can really be restored when you need it.
probe.never: No probe restore has run yet.

disabled.short: Keys of another system are disabled on this server.
disabled.title: Restoring a backup of another system is switched off
disabled.intro: This backup was made by another system, so it can only be read with that system’s encryption key. Entering such a key is switched off on this server.
disabled.step1: Open the .env file of this installation (next to docker-compose.yml) and add this line:
disabled.step2: Apply it by running this command in the same folder (a plain “docker compose restart” does NOT re-read the .env file):
disabled.step3: Reload this page. A field for the encryption key then appears here.
disabled.warning: Security: while this switch is on, a SUPER_ADMIN can run arbitrary SQL as the database user (a restore executes the contents of the archive as the database superuser, and a SUPER_ADMIN can build an archive under their own key). Enable it only for the migration and only if all SUPER_ADMINs are fully trusted. Afterwards remove the line from .env and run the command again.

sourceKey.summary: Backup from another system? Enter its encryption key
sourceKey.hint: Paste the complete APP_ENCRYPTION_KEYS value of the source system (all entries, e.g. k1:...,k0:...). The key is used on the server only for this step and is never shown again. It also works when the source system used the same key id as this one. After the restore the key is kept in a protected file on the data volume as an additional key that can only decrypt, until the secrets were re-encrypted (below).
sourceKey.label: Encryption key(s) of the source system

results.readable: This backup is already readable with this system's own keys; no other key is needed.
results.disabled: Keys of another system are disabled on this server.
results.unknown: This backup was made with a key id that is not among the entered keys. Enter the complete key ring of the source system.
results.mismatch: The key does not match this backup (or the file is damaged).
results.invalid: The entered text is not a valid key. Expected entries like id:base64 (32 bytes), separated by commas or lines.
results.notBackup: This file is not a backup archive.
results.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Please wait a few minutes.

sourceKey.otherSystem: This backup was made by another system and cannot be read with this system’s key. Enter the encryption key of that system here: the value of APP_ENCRYPTION_KEYS from its .env file (for example k1:AbC…=).
sourceKey.otherSystemUpload: A rejected upload is deleted: upload the file again and enter the key in the upload dialog.

reencrypt.label: Re-encrypt all secrets with this system’s key afterwards (recommended)
reencrypt.hint: Decrypts the restored secrets (bank access, API keys, signing keys, settings) with the source key, stores them under this system’s own key and then removes the source key from this system. Backups made before that (including the one you restore now) still need the source key.

sourceKey.stillMissing: Note: {count, plural, one {# key} other {# keys}} that the secrets of this backup use are still missing, even with the entered keys.

additionalKeys.title: Additional decryption keys are active
additionalKeys.text: Secrets restored from another system (bank access, API keys, ticket signing keys, settings) are still encrypted with these additional keys: {ids}. They are kept in a protected file on the data volume and can only decrypt; new data is encrypted with this system’s own key. “Re-encrypt now” moves every stored secret to this system’s key and removes the additional keys afterwards. Backups made before that still need the source system’s key.

reencrypt.title: Re-encrypt all secrets with this system’s key
reencrypt.description: Every stored secret that still needs an additional key is decrypted and encrypted again with this system’s key. Only when everything was converted and verified are the additional keys removed. The shop keeps running meanwhile.
reencrypt.backupsNote: Backups made before this step (scheduled, manual and the uploaded foreign one) still contain secrets under the old key: keep the source system’s key for them.
reencrypt.passkeyHint: Instead of a code you can confirm with your passkey.

last.title: Last re-encryption
last.complete: Complete: the additional keys were removed ({keys}).
last.incomplete: Incomplete: {remaining} secrets could not be converted, the additional keys were kept.

reencrypt.keysUsedByBackups: {count, plural, =0 {None of the listed backups refers to the additional keys.} one {# listed backup holds secrets under the additional keys that will be removed.} other {# listed backups hold secrets under the additional keys that will be removed.}} {count, plural, =0 {} other {Restoring them later only works if you keep the key of the system that made them; otherwise their secrets stay unreadable.}}
reencrypt.acknowledge: I understand that the additional keys are removed and older backups then need the source system's key.
reencrypt.backupsUnchecked: {count, plural, one {# older backup carries} other {# older backups carry}} no key information and cannot be checked; keep the source system's key for them to be safe.

unreadableSecrets.title: Stored secrets cannot be read
unreadableSecrets.text: {count, plural, one {# stored secret} other {# stored secrets}} (for example mail, payment or bank credentials) cannot be opened with the encryption keys of this system. Restore the backup again and enter the encryption key of the system that made it, or enter the affected credentials anew in the settings. After you entered them, use "Check again".

reencryptPending.title: Re-encryption pending
reencryptPending.text: The re-encryption queued after the restore has not run yet. Until it has, the restored secrets still depend on the additional keys.
reencryptPending.textGaveUp: The re-encryption queued after the restore could not start because another backup operation kept running. Start it by hand with "Re-encrypt now" once that operation has finished.
